features.02a7818a6ee0: This page describes Freally Oscillate as it will be at version 1.0 — the rung the ladder ends on — and nothing planned after it.
features.07e3bfdc40c6: Sixty-nine devices, among them Freally Secretarium and its 1 648 instruments. Each panel is drawn from the device's own description, so the number on a knob is the number the audio is using, and a device's settings copy as one line you can paste into a chat.

features.1b20c8037295: Freally Oscillate as it will be at version 1.0, beside seven commercial products as they are sold on 1 October 2026 — taken from each one's own product pages, shop, manual and support articles. Prices are list prices in US dollars.
features.1bcf2a5c1071: Hold more than four producers in a room. The fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out.
features.1c72614b8ea2: No account and no telemetry. It uses the network on three occasions only: a room you opened or joined, the address lookup while that room is set up, and an update check that is off until you switch it on. Crash reports stay on your disk unless you choose to send one.

features.389cb06662bc: Side by side with the leading DAWs
features.3ab5583a8c27: The companion folder writes stems and MIDI that any other DAW can open, lined up at bar 1, in the format, sample rate and bit depth you choose.

features.b4a6bff8b8c9: Every figure is a count of what version 1.0 carries. Nothing is estimated and nothing is rounded up. Freally Secretarium plays the same instrument library as Freally MIDI Master: one library, pinned by both, rather than two copies that drift apart.

features.b9277cfd1dc1: Unlimited audio and MIDI tracks, clips drawn from what they are, automation on every fader, pan and device control, comping, groups, markers, and tempo and time-signature maps. features.cut.body: Draw a blade stroke across the arrangement and it splits every clip it crosses; the angle of the stroke sets the crossfade slope. It is the motion language the whole interface is built on.
features.cut.title: The Cut
features.d2a4cd186952: Every edit is an operation in one log. Undo, the room's sync, Session Rewind and the Split Sheet are four readings of it, which is why your undo can be yours alone and why credit can be derived rather than typed in.
features.d32646eadd7e: Share a screen from macOS. Screen share is Windows and Linux; on macOS the button is absent and says why.
features.d3a91a73c5cc: A beat battle mode in which each turn owns its own bars. The countdown is a countdown; the bars are the rule, so two computers can never disagree about whose edit was legal.
features.d48bbcde1043: apps for Windows and macOS; Linux in a browser
features.d65f870603be: Knobs, faders and buttons rendered in Blender, five skins in light and dark beside both themes, short interface sounds you can switch off, and eighteen languages with real right-to-left — the same look in every Freally app.
features.d6f79cef6f38: instruments and effects of its own
features.da9afac0d7b7: It is free today. All of it.
features.db3a0428cdec: No model, no inference, nothing generative. A build gate walks the dependency graph and fails on any inference runtime or model file, so it is a property of the build rather than a sentence on a website.
features.dbdcc26cbc1a: Freally Oscillate 1.0 and seven commercial DAWs, feature by feature
features.devices.body: Sixty-nine instruments and effects, with panels drawn from the device's own description — so the number on the knob is the number the audio is using, measured to a tenth of a decibel.
features.devices.title: Its own instruments
features.e5498b8a441d: The short version: every other product on that table asks for an account, and each asks for money for its full feature set. Two of them let several people edit one project — Pro Tools track by track through its cloud, Soundtrap live in its own cloud. Oscillate puts four producers in one arrangement live, peer to peer, with no account, and it is free today.
features.ef0a07e0d7a5: One shortcut renders a 1200×630 picture of the session to post. Session Timelapse rebuilds the whole session from its edit log as an animated picture with chapters — even a session nobody thought to record.
features.f997324cb19b: Every feature, for everyone. No paid tier, no trial that runs out, no licence key, no account and no in-app purchase.
features.fc8d60587699: Usable with no account at all
features.free.body: No tier, no trial, no account, no licence key. No model, no inference, no "smart" anything — and that is enforced by a build gate that fails on any ML runtime entering the dependency graph, not left as a promise.
features.free.title: Free, and no AI
features.kumite.body: A beat battle mode where each turn owns its own bars, and an authorship ledger derived from the edit log with work anybody undid netted out.
features.kumite.title: Kumite and the Split Sheet
features.pianoRoll.body: Around ninety scales with highlighting, snapping and folding, ghost notes from any other clip, a velocity lane with per-note handles, and a playable keyboard where one key plays a whole chord.
features.pianoRoll.title: The piano roll
features.plugins.body: VST3 and CLAP, each in a process of its own, so a plugin that crashes greys out a device instead of losing your session. Graph-wide delay compensation, proved by a null test rather than asserted.
features.plugins.title: Plugin hosting
features.room.body: Up to four producers, peer to peer, with no account and no server. Live cursors, chat, voice, camera tiles and screen share. Your undo takes back your change and never somebody else's.
features.room.title: The room
features.title: What is in it

hero.headline: One session. Four producers. No server.
hero.tagline: A DAW where four producers work in the same session at once.
honest.ai.body: A build gate walks the dependency graph and fails on any inference runtime, any model file, and any analytics or crash-reporting library. It is a property of the build rather than a sentence on a website.
honest.ai.title: No AI, and how that is enforced
honest.code.body: It is the connection offer itself, and it carries your computer's public address. Treat it like a password: send it to the people you are working with and nobody else. The application says so at the moment you copy one.
honest.code.title: What a room code actually contains
honest.downloads.body: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. A DAW that half-works is worse than one that is not there yet.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads before 1.0.0
honest.failure.body: Some networks hand every outbound connection a different address, and two of those cannot find each other without a relay in the middle. A relay costs bandwidth forever, and that is a running bill a free application cannot carry — so Oscillate ships without one and lets you put your own in Settings. When a connection fails it names which of the nine causes it was.
honest.failure.title: Roughly one connection in ten will not form
honest.peers.body: A room holds four people. There is no server relaying audio, so every peer sends to every other peer, and the fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out. Four is the number that works rather than the number that sounded good.
honest.peers.title: Four producers, and not five
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.updater.body: An update check, and only when you press the button or switch on checking at launch — it is off by default. It asks for one static file and sends nothing about you or your machine, every update is signed, and none is ever installed without your choice.
honest.updater.title: The one connection the application makes

site.tagline: A DAW where four producers work in the same session at once.
what.p1: Every DAW is single-player software. Making a record with someone in another country still means exporting stems, uploading them, waiting, re-importing, and losing the thread — and six months later nobody remembers who wrote the bassline.
what.p2: Oscillate is a full DAW built around the opposite assumption. You paste a room code into a chat and up to three other producers drop into your session: you see their cameras, you hear them, their cursors move on your timeline, and when you are finished it prints a split sheet saying who wrote what.
what.p3: It is free today, and there is no server behind it. The room code is the connection offer, so the first person to join pastes a code and after that the room relays for everybody else. Nothing to keep running, nothing to pay for, nothing anybody can switch off.
